You are a hostile staff SRE reviewing a change to a live product run by one person.
Find the specific failure this change causes in production. Be concrete: name the
mechanism, the trigger, the user-visible symptom. Reject generic risk language.
If the change is genuinely safe, say so plainly and briefly.

# Context

ThePickleHub: bilingual VI/EN pickleball platform, ~2000 real users, solo-built.
Web (React/Vite on Cloudflare Pages) serves all 2000 users and is already bilingual.
There is a separate native iOS app source tree at `apple/` (SwiftUI, ~199 Swift files).

Distribution facts I verified:
- The App Store listing (id 6759968026, bundleId `net.thepicklehub.app`, v1.0.1,
  min iOS 15) is an OLD Capacitor WebView app that just loads the website.
- The `apple/` SwiftUI app is a DIFFERENT product: `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER:
  net.thepicklehub.app.dev`, deploymentTarget iOS 17.0. It is NOT distributed —
  simulator and local device builds only. No TestFlight evidence in repo.
- Project is generated by xcodegen 2.45.4 from `apple/project.yml`. Xcode 26.3.
- Test baseline: 154 tests / 31 suites green, run via xcodebuild CLI.

# The proposed change

Convert the `apple/` SwiftUI app from Vietnamese-only to bilingual VI+EN using a
Xcode String Catalog (`.xcstrings`). Language follows iOS Settings (per-app language
picker); NO in-app toggle. Do the whole thing in ONE batch: ~151 files that contain
Vietnamese text, estimated ~1000 string literals, estimated 3-5 half-days including
writing the English translations and reviewing them. 1-2 large PRs.

Current config: `apple/project.yml` has `DEVELOPMENT_LANGUAGE: vi` and
`SWIFT_EMIT_LOC_STRINGS: "YES"`. There is currently NO .xcstrings, NO .lproj,
and ZERO calls to `NSLocalizedString` or `String(localized:)` anywhere.

# What I measured myself in the repo (treat as ground truth)

1. Actual count of Vietnamese string literals: **1766**, not ~1000.
2. I classified each by its syntactic position:
   - **790** sit in positions typed `LocalizedStringKey` (`Text("...")`,
     `Button("...")`, `.navigationTitle("...")`, `.alert("...")`,
     `.accessibilityLabel("...")`). These auto-extract into the catalog and
     auto-localize.
   - **976** sit in positions typed plain `String`. Examples:
     - Computed properties in the model layer:
       `var label: String { self == .doubles ? "Đôi" : "Đơn" }`
       `switch code { case "setup": return "Đang cài đặt" ... }`
       (181 such literals in the Core/ model layer alone)
     - Arguments to the project's own design-system components, which declare
       `let title: String` / `let label: String` / `let placeholder: String`:
       `TLEmptyState(icon: "ticket", title: "Không tìm thấy đăng ký", subtitle: "...")`
       `TLPrimaryButton(title: "Đăng nhập") { ... }`
       `TLTextField(placeholder: "Mật khẩu", text: $password, isSecure: true)`
       Internally these do `Text(title)` where `title: String`.
     - String concatenation / interpolation building sentences from VI fragments.
3. I built a minimal reproduction with the same project.yml settings and confirmed:
   - xcodegen 2.45.4 DOES add `.xcstrings` correctly (`lastKnownFileType =
     text.json.xcstrings`, into the Resources build phase).
   - The built .app contains only `en.lproj/Localizable.strings`; no `vi.lproj`
     (source language stays as keys in the binary). `CFBundleDevelopmentRegion = vi`.
     At runtime `Bundle.main.localizations == ["en", "vi"]`, so the per-app language
     picker will appear.
   - `String(localized: "Đăng nhập")` returns "Sign in" under AppleLanguages=(en). Good.
   - `Mode.random.rawValue` (an `enum Mode: String { case random = "Ngẫu nhiên" }`)
     returns "Ngẫu nhiên" unchanged, as expected.

# Specific code sites I found

- `apple/ThePickleHub/Features/Profile/AccountSettingsView.swift:103` — account
  deletion confirmation. The alert shows `TextField("Nhập XOÁ để xác nhận", ...)`
  and the destructive button is
  `.disabled(deleteText.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).uppercased() != "XOÁ")`.
- `apple/ThePickleHub/Features/Bracket/DoublesElimRegistrationView.swift:222` —
  after registering a doubles team:
  `if model.regMessage?.hasPrefix("Đăng ký thành công") == true { partner = nil; teamName = "" }`
  The producer is `DoublesElimDetailView.swift:100`:
  `regMessage = "Đăng ký thành công" + (avg.map { String(format: " · DUPR %.2f", $0) } ?? "")`
- `apple/ThePickleHub/Core/DoublesElim/DoublesElimRepository.swift:311` — team name
  sent to the server when creating a tournament:
  `let derived = team.teamName.trimmed.nonEmpty ?? (!p1.isEmpty && !p2.isEmpty ? "\(p1) / \(p2)" : (p1.nonEmpty ?? p2.nonEmpty ?? "Đội"))`
  then `DEAtomicCreateTeam(team_name: derived, ...)` is POSTed to a Supabase RPC.
  The same rows are rendered on the public website.
- `apple/ThePickleHub/Features/Bracket/TeamMatchDetailView.swift:1366` —
  `enum Mode: String, CaseIterable { case random = "Ngẫu nhiên", manual = "Thủ công" }`,
  used only as `@State private var mode: Mode` and rendered via
  `ForEach(Mode.allCases, id: \.self) { Text($0.rawValue).tag($0) }`. Not persisted,
  not sent to the server.
- Tests asserting Vietnamese strings verbatim (will fail on translation):
  `Tests/UserFacingErrorTests.swift:13,23`, `Tests/TournamentMutationErrorTests.swift:11,18`,
  `Tests/MatchmakingTests.swift:89,90`, `Tests/DraftStoreTests.swift:21`.
- `apple/ThePickleHub/Core/Social/Matchmaking.swift:277-289` — `scheduleToText()`
  builds a Vietnamese plain-text match schedule ("Vòng 1", "Sân 2: A vs B",
  "Ngồi ngoài: ...") that is copied to `UIPasteboard` for the organizer to paste
  into Zalo (a Vietnamese chat app) for their players.

# Questions

1. What breaks in production? Be specific about which of these is real vs cosmetic.
2. Is the "one batch, 3-5 half-days" plan sound given the 790/976 split?
3. What failure mode am I NOT seeing? Especially: anything about String Catalog
   extraction, plural/grammatical agreement, iOS per-app language behaviour,
   or the interaction between a translated client and a shared server database
   whose rows are rendered by the (separately localized) website.
4. Rank the risks. Tell me plainly if this is low-risk.
